correctness.rationale: Direct multiplication of two general strictly upper-triangular 4x4 matrices yields precisely the six equations in RESULT.md. Four disjoint cases exhaust all square-one elements, with valid counts and independent cardinality sum; the weighted centralizer sum simplifies to q^8+2q^7−2q^5. Symbolic proof applies to every finite even field; independent direct matrix multiplication exhausts q=2 and q=4 as corroboration.

value.rationale: The natural two-point refinement of the classical finite-field square-zero count is completely determined at the first upper-unitriangular dimension with nilpotency class three. The four restricted-centralizer populations explain an unexpected nonzero 1/4 limiting commuting probability via competing maximal-dimensional square-zero components. This exact rank-four cutoff is mathematically motivated by the first additional quadratic relation and is not presented as an arbitrary isolated statistic or an all-rank classification.
